source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Handshaking lemma
statement: The sum of vertex degrees equals twice the number of edges; hence the number of odd-degree vertices is even.
conditions: G is a finite undirected graph, with loops counted twice.
conclusion: sum_v d(v)=2|E| and odd-degree vertices occur in an even count.
typical_uses: Prove parity constraints and impossibility results.
common_misuses: Counting a loop once in its incident vertex degree.
repair_templates: Write the incidence sum edge by edge.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Euler trail criterion
statement: A connected graph has an Euler circuit iff every vertex has even degree; it has an Euler trail with distinct endpoints iff exactly two vertices have odd degree.
conditions: All nonisolated vertices lie in one connected component.
conclusion: The degree parity characterizes existence of an edge-covering trail.
typical_uses: Construct or rule out Euler tours.
common_misuses: Ignoring disconnected isolated vertices or repeating edges.
bridge_lemmas: Follow unused edges and splice closed walks.
repair_templates: Check connectivity of the nonisolated subgraph and odd-degree count.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Equivalent tree characterizations
statement: For a finite graph, being connected and acyclic is equivalent to having n-1 edges, unique paths between vertices, and minimal connectivity.
conditions: G is a finite simple graph on n vertices.
conclusion: Any one standard tree characterization implies the others.
typical_uses: Recognize spanning trees and prove edge counts.
common_misuses: Using n-1 edges alone without connectivity.
bridge_lemmas: Deleting an edge from a tree disconnects it; adding an edge creates a cycle.
repair_templates: Pair the edge count with connectivity or acyclicity.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Bipartite iff no odd cycle
statement: A graph is bipartite iff it contains no odd cycle.
conclusion: A two-coloring exists exactly when every cycle has even length.
typical_uses: Test bipartiteness and construct two-colorings by BFS parity.
common_misuses: Checking only triangles and overlooking longer odd cycles.
bridge_lemmas: Distances from a root define parity classes in each component.
repair_templates: Run a parity coloring and identify a same-color edge as an odd cycle witness.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Kuratowski criterion
statement: A finite graph is planar iff it contains no subdivision of K5 or K3,3.
conclusion: Nonplanarity is certified by a subdivision of one of the two forbidden graphs.
typical_uses: Prove graph nonplanarity and analyze embeddings.
common_misuses: Using minors or subgraphs without allowing edge subdivision correctly.
bridge_lemmas: Suppress degree-two vertices in a subdivision to recover the forbidden graph.
repair_templates: Exhibit branch vertices and internally disjoint replacement paths.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Menger theorem vertex form
statement: The maximum number of internally vertex-disjoint u-v paths equals the minimum size of a vertex separator separating u from v.
conditions: u and v are distinct vertices in a finite graph.
conclusion: Path packing and vertex-cut size are equal.
bridge_lemmas: Transform vertex capacities to edge capacities by vertex splitting.
repair_templates: Specify whether endpoints may overlap and whether separators exclude u,v.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Hall marriage theorem
statement: A bipartite graph has a matching saturating the left part iff every subset S of the left part has at least |S| neighbors.
conclusion: The neighborhood condition is necessary and sufficient for a system of distinct representatives.
typical_uses: Prove existence of matchings and assignments.
common_misuses: Checking Hall's condition only for singletons.
bridge_lemmas: Augmenting-path argument repairs a nonmaximum matching.
repair_templates: Quantify over every subset S of the designated side.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Tutte perfect matching theorem
statement: A finite graph has a perfect matching iff for every vertex subset S, the number of odd components of G-S is at most |S|.
conditions: G is a finite undirected graph.
conclusion: The odd-component condition exactly characterizes perfect matchability.
typical_uses: Test perfect matchings in nonbipartite graphs.
common_misuses: Counting components of G rather than G-S.
bridge_lemmas: Every perfect matching pairs odd components through S.
repair_templates: Form G-S for arbitrary S and count its odd connected components.

source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Greedy coloring bound
statement: Every graph has a proper coloring with at most Delta+1 colors, where Delta is maximum degree; an ordering can improve the bound when a low-degree vertex exists.
conditions: G is a finite graph with maximum degree Delta.
conclusion: A greedy sequential coloring uses at most Delta+1 colors.
typical_uses: Construct explicit colorings and upper-bound chromatic number.
common_misuses: Claiming Delta colors without additional structure.
bridge_lemmas: At most Delta colors are forbidden at each vertex when colored last.
repair_templates: Choose an ordering and count already colored neighbors.
